metadata.title: Coupled hydro-mechanical simulation in the carbonate reservoir of a giant oil field in southwest Iran
metadata.description: The Asmari reservoir in southwest Iran has been producing oil continuously for over 50 years. However, due to an essential pressure decline, the reservoir is now a potential candidate for injection projects. The geomechanical analysis is essential for a successful injection operation to enhance reservoir production and address possible challenges. An accurate estimation of the injection pressure is necessary to maintain optimal conditions during the injection process and reduce possible risks. In this work, a coupled reservoir-geomechanical model, as well as rock mechanical tests, is performed to evaluate not only pressure variation and the associated in situ stress changes but also their potential influences on fault reactivation, reservoir–caprock stability, and surface displacement. For geomechanical evaluation, empirical correlations are derived between static and dynamic rock properties based on core data and existing petrophysical logs for the studied reservoir–caprock system. Based on the hydro-mechanical results, the maximum displacement is limited to the vicinity of the injection wells, where the highest pressure changes occur. The geomechanical analysis of the reservoir–caprock system shows that this system is stable until the injection pressure reaches 4.3× the initial reservoir pressure. Also, the injection pressure is not high enough to compromise the integrity of faults, indicating that the loading on the fault planes is too low to reactivate the pre-existing faults. The approach followed in this study can be applied to future field development strategies and feasibility considerations for CO2 sequestration and underground gas storage projects.

metadata.title: SaraEl-Metwally/Concrete-strength-prediction: v2.0.0 - Initial Production Release
metadata.description:
Concrete Strength Prediction

This project provides a machine learning solution for predicting the compressive strength of concrete mixtures based on their composition and age. It includes:

  • Model training scripts for building and evaluating regression models.
  • A modern desktop GUI for interactive predictions.
  • A FastAPI backend for web-based or API access.

Project Structure

concrete-strenght-prediction/
│
├── app.py                # FastAPI backend for predictions
├── gui.py                # PyQt5 desktop GUI application
├── model-training.py     # Model training and evaluation script
├── preprocessing.py      # Feature engineering and preprocessing functions
├── requirements.txt      # Python dependencies
├── saved/
│   ├── models/           # Trained model files (.joblib)
│   ├── assets/           # Evaluation plots, SHAP explanations, etc.
│   └── preprocessing/    # Encoders (if any)
├── data/
│   └── Concrete_Data.xls # Raw dataset
└── static/
    └── index.html        # Frontend for FastAPI (if used)

Installation

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/Ahmed-Hereiz/Concrete-strength-prediction.git
cd concrete-strenght-prediction

  2. Install dependencies:

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Prepare the dataset:

    • Place Concrete_Data.xls in the data/ directory.

Model Training

To train and evaluate the models:

python model-training.py
  • This will preprocess the data, train several regression models, save them in saved/models/, and generate evaluation plots and SHAP explanations in saved/assets/.

Using the Desktop GUI

The GUI allows interactive prediction of concrete strength:

python gui.py
  • Adjust mixture parameters using sliders.
  • Select a prediction model.
  • View predicted strength and feature details.

Requirements: PyQt5 (installed via requirements.txt).

Using the FastAPI Backend

Start the API server:

python app.py
  • The API will be available at http://localhost:8000.
  • The main page (if static/index.html exists) is served at /.
  • Prediction endpoint: POST /predict

Requirements

  • Python 3.7+
  • See requirements.txt for all dependencies (scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, PyQt5, fastapi, uvicorn, lightgbm, shap, etc.)

Notes

  • Models must be trained before using the GUI or API (saved/models/ must exist).
  • Feature engineering is handled via preprocessing.py.
  • SHAP explanations and evaluation plots are generated for model interpretability.

metadata.title: pyALDIC-3D: stereo / 3D Digital Image Correlation built on the pyALDIC platform
metadata.description: pyALDIC-3D is an independent, self-contained desktop application and headless CLI for stereo (two-camera) Digital Image Correlation. It reconstructs full-field 3D shape, displacement, and Green-Lagrange surface strain from synchronized stereo image sequences, using the Augmented-Lagrangian DIC engine of the pyALDIC 2D platform (al-dic) and following the MATLAB 3D-Stereo-ALDIC reference implementation as its mathematical model. Features include built-in QC-instrumented stereo calibration (chessboard, ChArUco, circle-grid, coded circular targets, plus 6 import formats), three pluggable correspondence strategies, crack-aware DIC, an interactive PyVista 3D view, NPZ/MAT/CSV/PLY/VTU export, an 8-language GUI, and a TOML-driven batch CLI.

metadata.title: Background Subtraction Using MuscleX: Sample Data And Tutorial
metadata.description: The archive provides a tutorial and two sample patterns for reproducing the background subtraction results described in the manuscript "A Framework for Global Background Subtraction in Fiber Diffraction Patterns from Striated Muscle" using MuscleX's Quadrant Folding module. The README.pdf file covers two background subtraction approaches: (1) non-parametric optimization between a set of commonly used methods (Circularly-symmetric, Roving Window, 2D Convexhull, White-top-hats, and Smoothed-Gaussian/BoxCar) and (2) iterative parametric fitting of the equatorial streak and general background. The tutorial covers the GUI workflow and the CLI commands to reproduce the results.

metadata.title: LAMMPS-GUI
metadata.description: LAMMPS-GUI is a cross-platform Qt-based graphical application for the LAMMPS molecular dynamics simulation software. It integrates an input-script editor, live simulation execution via the LAMMPS C-library interface, log and thermodynamic-data viewing, interactive plotting, and snapshot/slide-show visualization into a single tool aimed at learning and exploring molecular dynamics with LAMMPS.

metadata.title: MarsCONE 2.0: A toolbox for automatic detection of Martian and terrestrial pitted cones morphology
metadata.description:
MarsCONE 2.0: Desktop GUI for End-to-End Volcanic Cone Morphometry

This release provides MarsCONE 2.0, a PySide6 desktop application that orchestrates the full morphometric workflow for volcanic cone analysis from DEM-based inputs. The GUI integrates pipeline execution, quality control, manual correction, complex-cone aggregation, and cross-dataset comparison in a single interface.

MarsCONE 2.0 is implemented as a thin desktop layer over the existing core modules. Instead of executing core code in place, the application creates an isolated runtime session, generates fresh module configurations, and executes copied modules in that temporary workspace. This design improves run reproducibility and reduces the risk of accidental edits to development sources.

Main Features

  • End-to-end execution of generator, finder, and analyzer modules (individually or as a full pipeline).
  • Interactive QA tools for cross-sections and DEM overlays.
  • Manual correction workflow for finder key points, with downstream analyzer reprocessing support.
  • Complex-cone workflow for grouped systems, including topology summaries and merged DEM outputs.
  • Exploratory visualization tools for single-dataset trends and distributions.
  • Multi-dataset comparison module (scatter, heatmap, embedding, similarity/statistics exports).

Reproducibility and Runtime Model

  • Module runs are executed in isolated runtime session folders.
  • Runtime configuration files are generated from the current GUI state.
  • Logs are streamed and preserved through the application interface.
  • Output conventions are standardized across pipeline and QA products.

Installation and Environment Use Python environment that runs the core MarsCONE modules, including the scientific/geospatial stack and PySide6. A video tutorial is available: https://youtu.be/1dHleOnAUo8

Workflow tutorial A video tutorial is available: https://youtu.be/yoiDoCZxY9g

The latest release, v2.0.1, includes corrections to the readme and provides more detailed information on QA in the Analyzer module.

metadata.title: Mantid Imaging
metadata.description: Mantid Imaging is a graphical toolkit for performing 3D reconstruction of neutron tomography data.  It provides an easy-to-use graphical interface to a wide range of pre/post-processing operations, tilt correction and reconstruction algorithms, accommodating for tomography users with varying data complexity and image analysis background knowledge. It utilises a flexible plugin system that allows easy integration of external software, and has allowed us to re-use software widely known in the neutron tomography community.

metadata.title: Minimum-Intervention Zero-Mode Removal via Inverse Matrix Rigidity
metadata.description:
Zero modes play a central role in mechanical metamaterials, topological mechanics, and constraint networks. This preprint develops a complementary minimum-intervention interpretation based on inverse matrix rigidity. For a square singular matrix CCC, its nullity is interpreted as the exact minimum number of independently modifiable matrix entries required to restore full rank in the unconstrained entry-level model.

Building on the author’s prior inverse-rigidity theorem, the paper introduces the entry-support admissibility gap V(C,Ω)V(C,\Omega)V(C,Ω), a three-regime classification of matrix–entry-support pairs, an exact matching–minor characterization of restricted rank restoration, physical-operation rigidity, a zero-mode overlap identity, and an exact unstructured zero-mode reappearance radius. It also establishes connections with Maxwell–Calladine counting and chiral Hamiltonians and develops a grounding–connectivity criterion for spring networks.

The theory is illustrated through a path-graph spring network and the fully dimerized open Su–Schrieffer–Heeger chain. The accompanying Python GUI, verify_zero_mode_removal_gui.py, reproduces the finite-dimensional examples, verifies the matching–minor criterion and the reappearance radius, and permits predefined, manually entered, and randomly generated matrices of different sizes.

Supplementary files include the graphical verification program, its README, dependency specification, and software license. The underlying inverse-rigidity theorem and the previously published general-purpose calculator are cited as separate prior contributions.
